data.name: Divanshi
data.gender_notes: Divanshi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dhanvantari, the God of Ayurvedic Medicine, is believed to have carried the Amrita (nectar of immortality) in a pot named Divansa. Derived from this, the name Divanshi signifies the one who carries the divine nectar. The name Divanshi carries the meaning “Goddess of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Divanshi usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Divanshi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Divanshi total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.spiritual_significance: Divanshi signifies the one who carries the divine nectar of life, love, and wisdom. The name evokes a deep sense of spiritual awakening, the search for eternal bliss and spiritual well-being. It represents the journey towards inner purity and self-realization. The name Divanshi transcends beyond an ordinary name, it is a divine blessing that resonates with the soul's deepest desires and yearnings for spiritual growth and transformation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Divanshi: Dive meaning 'to immerse' and Ansh meaning 'soul'. Thus, Divanshi symbolizes one who immerses deeply into the soul or spirit.

historical_references.reference: Divanshi is believed to be the daughter of King Sahasrarjuna of Haihayas, mentioned in the Mahabharata. She is famously known as the 'Mahakali' or the great goddess Kali in her benevolent form.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic which forms a major part of Hindu mythology. The story of Divanshi is mentioned in the Anushasana Parva (Book of Instructions) of Mahabharata.

historical_references.reference: Divanshi is also the name of a goddess revered in the Jain faith. She is believed to be the goddess of virtue, peace, prosperity, and the embodiment of the Jain virtues of truth, non-violence, and compassion.
